utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, Colonel, as I indicate you have gone into some detail in these paragraphs, what I would like to ask you about and ask you to indicate on the map, and I'll leave it to you to chose to colour. The map, is P615, page 18 -- page 8 of the same -- or 18, pardon me, of the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, although you can give the witness hard copies and he can have more than one at a time, we can't see more than one thing at a time. I don't know how you're going to do this. If you're meaning us to flash back and forward, then fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, I guess --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- I'll read the English so that we can follow long with what the Colonel has in front of him, I think; but for that I'll need the English copy back if I could ask the usher. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, if you look at section 5.2 of this "zapovest" order for the Bajgora Bare action, it describes the blockade formed by one of your neighbouring friendly forces, the 15th Armoured Brigade, and the 5.2 in the "zapovest" it says: "The 15th Armoured Brigade 1st Motorised Battalion will set up a blockade along the line of the village of Breznice, south of Samodreza, village of Golubija, village of Smrekovnica and thereon it goes to describe that this was for purposes of preventing the spillover of terrorist forces from the village of Bajgora into Kosovo Polje." If you could please mark on the map, which I don't know if we have the map up yet, P615, page 18, I apologise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it's the map you want on the e-court screen, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Colonel --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we zoom in on this section of the map around Vucitrn which is in the upper middle of P615 to -- there we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, would you be in a position to mark on this map the blockade force -- the positions on the blockade formed by the 15th Armoured Brigade as set forth in 5.2 of the "zapovest," decision, and also based upon your personal knowledge and recollections of this action?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can't find Breznice, but the position of the brigade, its mechanised battalion, was to the right of the road, if you look at the Pristina-Mitrovica road. So it would be around here and then all the way up to Dreza itself. Specifically there is Golubija. My left wing was adjacent to this battalion in Kicici village.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that the dashed or broken line drawn initially was the blockade line and the solid line perpendicular to it in the upper left-hand corner is the line that was written in last -- that was written in last by the witness pertaining to his side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now -- one moment, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, the "zapovest" also talks about the village of Samodreza. I do not see that that is incorporated in the map you have drawn, is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, an objection. This witness cannot furnish relevant information on the positions of the 15th Brigade. This is mere speculation which is based on a document. He is the commander of the 58th Brigade. I believe he is able to do no more than to draw the positions and the movements of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had the same problem with General Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will need to deal with that in re-examination because he was asked if he would be in a position to mark it, and he said yes; so let's continue, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, just to be sure that your recollection and the illustration are complete, there is a reference to the region of the village of Samodreza. Is that description in the "zapovest" incorporated in this illustration on the map with respect to the line of the blockade where it says Grezice [phoen] village, village of Samodreza, village of Golubija, village of Smrekovnica.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to explain where the line would have been in relation to the Pristina-Mitrovica road. I wasn't there myself and, of course, I can't mark the position of each unit. I should perhaps point out that I'm speaking in roughest of terms. Maybe it's not exactly the location. You can't see all the villages in this map, but I'm talking about my right-hand neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to other neighbouring forces, another one that is not mentioned in your -- in your statement is the 54th Military Territorial Detachment which I believe was subordinated to the 15th Armoured Brigade. Do you actually have knowledge of where they were deployed in the area surrounding Vucitrn sector; if not, just let me know, and I can move on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I really don't think I could be definite about the position of the 54th Detachment. Some of their elements were close to Cicavica and there was one unit that I came across during the fighting on my right wing near Kicici, but they moved about as the situation required. I can't be definite about their precise location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, with respect to this particular action, that is to say the time-period of this action, which was I believe mid-April of 1999, would you be in a position to mark the known locations of armed resistance from terrorist forces that were encountered, perhaps using a different colour, which again I would leave to your discretion which colour to choose, since I know those are very important in terms of military map drafting.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the second half of April. This action was supposed to begin on the 27th, the 26th, or the 27th -- actually, it says here when it was completed. Siptar terrorist rebels were holding a sizeable share of the territory at the time. We should lower the map to show the north of this map to show the direction of Bajgora and Bare. If I can use blue because that's what I'm used to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We can't lower the map. Are there any on this sector that's now presently visible that you could mark for us; if not, then I will, I guess, save this image and perhaps move to the other sector on the map?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Before we zoomed in, I could actually see the northern section. I can mark the Siptar terrorist forces in my own area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take from your answer, sir, that you are not in a position to identify the terrorist forces that were in the southern part of your -- south of your forces where the blockade actually was? Is that -- am I understanding correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I can. I am in a position to do that in relation to my zone to the south of Kosovska Mitrovica. These would be positions as they were before the Bajgora action commenced.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as far as positions those would be only with respect to your zone? You're not representing that there were no forces in the zone of the blockade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: These are the Siptar terrorist forces in the area covered by the 58th Light Infantry Brigade that's marked in blue and then further up to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I guess could we have this saved as an IC number, and I think I will move on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC169, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Colonel, let's see, I can -- you can keep that order in front of you but I will not, I think, be referring to it again in our cross. With respect to another topic you discuss at paragraph 11 of your statement you discuss these military territorial detachments. I would like to ask you first briefly what specific detachments and from which regions were either in your zone of responsibility or resubordinated to you at some point in time during 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: The military territory division does not coincide with division into political communities so that in the zone of my brigade there are following detachments resubordinated from the military territorial area of Kosovska Mitrovica, 180th, 270th, and 271st; from that same military department of Kosovska Mitrovica the 54th was resubordinated to the 15th Armoured Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, for purposes of the transcript I thought I heard you say in the Serbian the 56th military territorial --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: 56th is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now with respect to these "odreds," at least the ones that were resubordinated -- strike that. The 54th was resubordinated to the 15th motorised -- Armoured Brigade of the VJ --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: To the 15th Armoured Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the remaining four "odreds," would I be correct that they came from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please use the English expression. It's -- makes the transcript impossible for us to read if you use expressions which are Serb and there's no translation available to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I'm listening to the witness rather than listening to myself when I say those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to these remaining four military territorial detachments, am I correct that they come from -- the 56th comes from Zubin Potok, the 180th from Kosovska Mitrovica, the 270th from Zvecan and the 271th from Leposavic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall the dates at which they were resubordinated to you, these four. I'm talking about just these four detachments?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Beginning of May, 1st, 2nd, or the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree that up until the time-period that they became resubordinated to your brigade, these military territorial detachments were engaged in tasks exclusively pursuant to the orders of the military district in Pristina and/or the military department in Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: They were under the command, until then the commander of the military department of Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you recall the numerical strength of these units that were under the command of the military department in Kosovska Mitrovica prior to being resubordinated to your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Not down to the last man, but the 56th and the 180th were company strong, equivalent of a battalion. The 270th and the 271st were platoons equivalent to a company, which means the first two had 200 to 300 and the other two had 100 to 120, maybe 150 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. And with respect to your own brigade, I know that it probably fluctuated during the war, but do you recall the manpower of your brigade as well as the breakdown between active and reserve components for the same at any point in time -- can you give us a reference for any point in time during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: This whole unit was not active, our brigade, that is, until the beginning of the war, it was not active. And from the beginning of the mobilisation drive, although mobilisation is an uninterrupted process, it was 70 per cent of establishment; up to the end of the war, we achieved 92 per cent of the establishment. Or in numbers 1400 to 1900 men together with resubordinated detachments, and there was also one artillery battalion of anti-aircraft defence that was resubordinated. I had a maximum of 3500 men under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already mentioned the anti-aircraft unit so I can actually skip two of my questions. Now, at paragraph 11 of your statement among the other assignments or tasks that you describe for your brigade, you have securing of main roadways. Can you identify for us which roadways are in question and how this assignment was to be undertaken.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: The priority road was Kosovska Mitrovica-Sipolje-Gornja Klina towards Srbica and towards Pec respectively. It was the hardest to secure, and in addition to that, there was the road Kosovska Mitrovica-Zubin Potok, which was in jeopardy in one period, and there were two more roads in my zone Kosovska Mitrovica-Vucitrn-Pristina and Kosovska Mitrovica-Leposavic-Raska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You identify that the roadways were in jeopardy, and I think in your statement you also discuss some of the hardships faced in the area. I would just like to highlight a couple of documents relating to that. If we can have 6D1489 up in e-court. Sir, I think you will see this to be a Pristina Corps command combat report dated the 17th of May, 1999, and on the -- I believe on the second page of the original, item 2.1, I believe you will see here a reference to members of your brigade carried out an anti-terrorist action clearing part of the surroundings of Kosovska Mitrovica of terrorists, and specifically we're talking about the sectors of the villages of Zabare, Tamnik, Sipovo. Do you recall how strong or how fierce of a resistance from the overall terrorist forces there was in this area at this time that this action was underway?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: This document does not speak of their defence; instead, they launched an action to cut off the road Mitrovica-Gornja Klina. They infiltrated their forces into these settlements, and at one point they cut off the road to which leads from the centre of the road -- centre of the town towards Sipolje and onwards. During that action, several civilians were killed and one of my military policemen. He was shot at from a house. There is a report covering this incident. I cannot recall it precisely, but this report exists. A 15-year-old boy grabbed the gun from the military policeman whom he had killed and ran away. We located that group later, and with the assistance of PJP units we managed to smash a part of them, whereas another part escaped across the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Am I correct that this region described here was the scene of earlier confrontations between -- I apologise, sir, the -- apparently I'm overlapping with the translation. Am I correct that this region that we've described here was the scene of earlier and, in fact, constant confrontations between the terrorist forces and the security forces, that is to say the forces of the state, in the time-period leading up to this action in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, certainly. But in that period the prior to was to remove the danger from Bajgora towards the old square; and later after the completion of Bajgora 2 action, but also because of those ever-more-frequent actions, we proceeded to resolve the problem in Kosovska Mitrovica itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we're focused on Kosovska Mitrovica, I'd like to show you another document to see if you are -- if you have any knowledge that you can assist us with this document, 6D1098, which is a, as you'll see, an order from the Kosovska Mitrovica military department dated I believe the 8th of May, 1999, regarding orders for maintaining of law and order. And once the document is up before you I would ask if, in fact, you are familiar with this document. And if you go on the last -- the second page or the last page I believe it will list, I think, the recipient information for the same.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: What am I supposed to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving this document or are you aware of the contents of this document detailing efforts to uphold law and order in the region of Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the document. It follows from the order of the corps commander. When the detachments were resubordinated to me, then the commander of the military department was appointed commander of the garrison. And order and discipline in the garrison was within his competence so that in that sense all of us were not subordinated but answerable to him because it was his legal obligation to remind us about the need to comply with order and discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. I think that helps us with this document. Now, sir, I'd like to move on to try and finish up if I can soon to Exhibit P2809, which is dated the 25th of April, 1999, strictly confidential number 455-183. This is a document from the command of the Pristina Corps relating to engagement of MUP forces. First of all, sir, do you recall receiving this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree that parts 1, 2, and 3 of the document, paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 advise the recipients of what -- strike that. Would you agree that parts 1, 2, and 3 of the document regulate which MUP units can be utilised in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I would direct your attention to paragraph 2 which references a plan for engagement identified as attachment 2. Since we don't have attachment 2 in e-court on this exhibit, I would ask that you be shown 6D1023, and that's a short document but I think you can analyse the same and let me know whether, in fact, this is the attachment 2 to the previous document which you received from your superior command. This is a plan for engagement of combined structures I believe is the translation. I don't have the English translation in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can just have the second page so the witness can have the benefit of the entire attachment, particularly the portion dealing with his brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you verify, in fact, that this was the plan for engagement that you received accompanying the previous exhibit listing the 35th -- 35th Detachment of the PJP as being the forces foreseen for utilisation by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this. It's an expression of those evaluations that a ground aggression is possible and that all forces in one zone be combined under one commander. Here the units of the MUP, specialised units, and other units which were under the secretariat of the interior could be subordinated in a particular zone. Under this order I made my own document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can go to that right now, sir. If it would help -- I believe I have your response at 6D1056, so perhaps we could short-circuit some of my preliminary questions if we go to that document we can then have you verify whether in fact that document is the document you're talking about, first of all, dated the 30th of April, 1999. Is this the -- is this your own document that you talk about that is a response to the plan that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Just a second. This is the 30th of April and the other one was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 25th of April I believe was the last document -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: So based on the previous document I drafted by own order and also on the map this was shown. I remember that the detachment got the assignment to carry out its regular tasks in the peacetime assignment. But in case of a ground invasion by NATO it would be engaged in the most threatened area along the most threatened axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can look at the last page of this exhibit, I believe that we'll see the 35th Detachment of the PJP and the tasks that you -- that you -- that you gave that formation. And I would just -- if you could verify that then I think your testimony is complete in that regard and I'll move on. Again, that's the last page of this exhibit. It should be -- one moment. We're having some difficulty in e-court. Just for sake of completeness, I think I'll have to have our -- have the document in e-court looked at, but if I could have the usher show the witness a hard copy of the same, my hard copy is five pages long, whereas the e-court appears to be just one page long, and if you could show him the last page I think he can quickly confirm that in fact the section for the 35th Detachment of the PJP is there and it comports with the section that you just testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you seen more than one page of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: No, I was just going to mention that, Your Honour, I have only seen the copy that's in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If there's only one page, that must be all that you uploaded, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what it sounds like. I'll have to probably upload a whole new exhibit. I have no problem with the hard copy being passed on to the Prosecution. It's -- unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do we have a version in English though because unfortunately I don't read B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would have to check. I see we have a translation of what was in e-court. It should have been all sent together. But things that are one exhibit don't always stay one exhibit when dealing with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you have a problem with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, also I don't have that document and I would like to see the other pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you're going to have the advantage over Ms. Kravetz. Can we have on the ELMO the part that you're going to refer to, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. It's the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And first of all, sir, would you confirm for us whether, in fact, this appears to be attachment 2 as referenced on the first page of your document, a plan for engagement of joint -- of combined structures it actually should be although the English says, I think, "joint"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: In the course of execution of actions, they would be a combined unit. That's the attachment, the plan of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And does the -- when you testified just a few moments ago as to the tasking of the PJP detachment, is that accurately reflected here; that is to say, is this the tasking that you're talking about? Is this document -- the document that you were referencing earlier?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. So they have to accomplish coordinated action with military territorial detachment --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down when he's reading this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just stop for a moment, please. The interpreter has -- is unable to keep up with your pace of reading, please. So, Mr. Savic, will have to read that again and read it more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. So there are several assignments listed here. Do you want me to read them all out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's a matter for Mr. Ivetic what he wants you to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think in fairness to the Prosecution I should have him read it so they know what this section of the document is since I don't have an English translation of the same. I apologise for the awkwardness of this, but I think that's the only way to be fair to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, please read it then, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document there are certain spelling mistakes, but I'll deal with that. So it begins: "Parts of the 35th Detachment of PJP -- sorry, 53rd PJP Detachment have certain assignments: Establish command and coordinated action with the 280th," and that's a mistake, "and uninterrupted functions of communications systems KM in Kosovo and Metohija, planned execution of defence in keeping with the decision of the brigade commander in the area Svinjare Halaca, Bair warehouse in coordinated action with the 53rd PJP Detachment. Then: "Detecting and destroying the remaining Siptar forces on following the routes: Vidusic, Bare, Bajgora, and Trstena, Cuca, Kovacica. Next: "Carry out continuous gathering of intelligence, processing of that intelligence, and report to the brigade commander about the enemies." Next: "Participating in the sanitization of the battle-field." Next: "Take measures to prevent disturbances, breaches of discipline, looting, robberies, desertion, arson, maltreatment, and other types of criminal acts within the units and in the territory of the area of responsibility as well as comply with the provisions of the international law of warfare." Next and the last: "Extend the necessary assistance with regard to the return of the population that had fled back to their homes, suggesting to them safer places than the area affected by combat activities."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, what is this document? I'm afraid I've lost my way here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is, if I can speak and if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, just you tell me what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is a document authored by this witness in response to the previous exhibit, and this document sets forth his plan for engagement of forces within his zone of responsibility. And the -- I fast forwarded to the last page which is the page that deals specifically with the MUP. The four prior pages which I think the witness can verify relate to other forces in his zone of responsibility, including the military territorial detachments that we've referenced earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Mr. Savic, is this drafted in the understanding that there will be resubordination of MUP units to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Throughout the war we were expecting that this would come through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And at one stage there you read: "Establish command and coordinated action with the 280th ..." And you said "that's a mistake." What was the mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says: "With 1180th and 280th." 1180th is the mistake. It should be 180th and 280th is correct, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just checking to see whether, in fact, the English transcript coincides with the -- with what the witness just said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for reading that document, again I apologise for not having translation of the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the interpreter's correction?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure anymore whether it's the 270th or the 280th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you're referring there to two organs, one is the 180th and the other is the 280th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I said it was a mistake. It says 1180. This first 1 is a mistake, so it's 180th Military Territorial Detachment. 280th does not exist; it should be 270th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's that point that was unclear and you've now clarified. Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, just to move on, you talk -- strike that. I want to ask you about some activities that occurred after this plan for resubordination and engagement was promulgated. Specifically, first of all, there is an action known as Prekaze, which I believe you do discuss in your statement, although it's not named as such. Are you familiar with this anti-terrorist action under the name Prekaz?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: The action's name is actually Prekaze.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that this is the action that you describe at paragraph 23 of your statement that actually took place at the end of May 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I stated in paragraph 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with respect to this action that both the 35th and the 36th PJP Detachments participated in the action alongside the VJ forces that were there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I can guarantee for the 35th Detachment which was with me, they were together with me, and we had very fierce firing from the other side. So as it says here, not nothing happened as planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is that due to several factors, including the desertion of the 7th Infantry Brigade and the attempt at cutting off the roadway by the terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was several unfavourable factors, unfavourable for our forces. It wasn't the entire brigade, but a detachment from that brigade which was my right-hand neighbour, looking in the north-south direction, left its positions. That area was vacated, so the Siptar terrorist forces filled it very quickly and they threatened the road from the village of Kucica to Brabonjic wishing to cut it off in that area. There was very fierce counter-fire from the direction of Hercegovo village in the direction of Sipovo and the Zmic feature. From there, they fired on the road and on vehicles and units moving along it. Therefore, we were unable to implement this and I informed the corps commander, General Lazarevic, about these new circumstances, and he accepted our arguments in favour of modifying the order that had already been issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I've just one more question with respect to this particular action that I will try to make as simple as possible. Am I correct that the 35th PJP Detachment that was engaged in this coordinated combat with your forces did not -- did -- strike that. That they did engage in the coordinated and concerted combat alongside your forces; that is, they went according to this modified plan that you presented?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We immediately with the commander of the detachment took appropriate measures to deal with the danger, the threat of cutting off the main road used to supply the forces in Kosovo and Metohija. So he engaged his companies in the Brabonjic-Kucica axis. And as my units were suffering fierce attacks by the Siptar terrorist forces, he responded to my request and engaged two of his companies at the very moment when the late Milosevic was killed at the Zmic feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to highlight a couple more areas and discuss the terrorist forces and strength in those areas within your zone. If I can have exhibit P2006 up on the screen. Colonel, I think you'll see that this is a combat report dated the 9th of May, 1999, and at section 2 on page 2 in the original Serb, and I think it's also in the English translation, you'll see that it describes that your forces along with the 125th Motorised Brigade and the 7th Infantry and 354th Infantry Brigades participated in a blockade of a region where the MUP was clearing the terrain and engaging the terrorist forces in accord with a -- with a decision of the commander of the Pristina Corps. Do you recall what region this action was undertaken in? And if it helps you any, I think under 2.7 it does reference some of the -- one of the participants, the 7th Infantry Brigade engaging and killing a terrorist in the sector of Zablace.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't recall. The 7th Brigade was to the south. In this period, that is, the 8th of May, we were engaged in the Bajgora 2 action to the north of where they were. But the same task that is mentioned in item 2.1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in your testimony previously. Let me just check one more detail, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I have no further documents or questions for you. Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you will now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Ms. Kravetz. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I believe you still have a copy with you of P1975, which is an order dated 15th April 1999. I wanted to ask you some questions regarding this order. You referred to it in paragraph 15 of your statement, and you say in your statement that you received this order along with other annexes in an envelope from the Pristina Corps command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You had the time to review this order when you were preparing your statement and today in court, so you have seen that at the top of this order it bears the heading "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija" and there's also a typed signature at the end of the order which says the same, "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija," correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you received this order in April of 1999, was this the first time you had seen such an order in this type of format or were you familiar with these types of orders bearing the heading "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: This document was already in the brigade command when I arrived, and that was the first time I had seen it with this heading, as stated here, Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, and that was the first time I came across it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I understand this is the first time you came across this specific order, but were you familiar with orders in this type of format bearing the heading "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. It was then that I first saw this kind of document with the heading "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija" in the course of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you know at the time what was the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: At the time we interpreted this to mean combined or joint commanding of units. So if I've managed to explain this, it is a Joint Command of forces of the MUP and the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Does that mean that generally speaking that orders that involved joint operations between the MUP and the army would bear this heading, Joint Command, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Those are my words, yes, but I don't think that later on we received any documents bearing the head Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija in the form of orders that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You went into quite some detail in your statement about how you went about implementing this order, and I'm curious to know, did you ask your commander, the Pristina Corps commander, why he had sent this order to you bearing the heading "Joint Command," why you were receiving instructions in this type of format?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask him that, but I think you'll see in my statement that pursuant to this order the commander of the 35th Detachment and I as the brigade commander went to Pristina together to ask for approval to carry out this task. The approval came from the instructions and the work of commands. When a subordinate commander understands a decision by his superior, he issues his own decision and he's duty-bound to ask for approval from his superior. That's why I didn't pay special attention to the heading "Joint Command."

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you did ask your superior about this order and why it had the heading "Joint Command" if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no, you misunderstood me. I didn't put the question to him why is this heading -- why does it read "Joint Command." I simply ask for his approval to implement item 5.3. I was not especially concerned about the heading. It didn't excite my attention, it didn't cause me to wonder what it meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But as you have seen in this order in paragraph -- item number 13, the second sentence which is at the end of the order, it expressly says that it is the Joint Command for Kosovo based in Pristina, which is to command and control all units in the course of combat operations. When you read this, this didn't strike you as odd, that there was a reference to the Joint Command commanding the combat operations in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't strike me as odd. If there was a decision on resubordination, then it was logical for the MUP command to be incorporated into the command of the Pristina Corps and to create some sort of Joint Command. At the time it didn't strike me as illogical.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You told us you had worked for sometime, a short time at corps command in Pristina. Are you aware who was in charge of or which department was in charge of drafting combat orders that were sent to troops on the ground?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was done by the department for staff affairs and training. The chief of that department at the time was Colonel Radojko Stefanovic; he was my immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And as you say in your statement that this order came in an envelope for the Pristina Corps command. So would it be correct to say that this order if it had come from the Pristina Corps command, it would have been drafted in the same department as other combat orders that were sent to VJ units on the ground?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So the drafter of those orders would have been Colonel Stefanovic, who was as you mentioned the chief of the department of staff affairs and training?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And during your time at the Pristina Corps command in Pristina you never came across any such type of order bearing the heading "Joint Command"? Mr. Stefanovic never gave you a copy of such order? You never saw it in the office?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, to avoid confusion, I was from that department with my section for training. When wartime actions started was something else. Sometimes I was an office courier taking post to Metohija or the forward command post. I participated in receiving units arriving from other units of the Army of Serbia in Kosovo, so that for the last three weeks in March or the last week in March and the first two weeks in April, I was on the ground; I was not in the command. That's why I don't how things developed in the staff or how things were done and in this department.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay, so I understand that your question to my question is no. Do you know when Colonel Stefanovic was appointed to that position of chief of department of staff affairs and training?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in that department on the 13th of January and I think he was appointed around the new year, around the 1st of January to the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall who was his predecessor prior to January 1999? Whom did he replace in that position?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Djakovic, who later became a general.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I want to move on a bit from this. We are continue with this document that's there before you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you move on, we've had a variety of expressions of understanding of the concept of "Joint Command." I want to be absolutely certain that I have not misunderstood you when you say that it was perfectly logical to create some sort of Joint Command if the MUP was to be resubordinated to the Pristina Corps. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's my standpoint that it would be logical for a Joint Command to be composed of officers both from the MUP and from the army. Your Honour, when I received detachments who were resubordinated to me from the Mitrovica military department, their representative or assistant commander for military territorial detachments joined my unit. So it would have been quite logical to unify this in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if I can follow-up on that question. You referred to this order saying that it was an order for joint actions between the VJ and the MUP. Your commander, General Lazarevic, could not on his own decide on the -- of joint actions with the MUP; is that correct? I mean, there would have had to have been some sort of coordination or planning at a higher level than yours for actions involving officers of the VJ and the MUP for such an action take place, correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: You have put a lot of questions. The corps commander cannot issue a decision on a Joint Command. Someone has to issue him with an order who he will coordinate with, just as he ordered me to coordinate with and support the MUP forces in the area assigned to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So just to be clear on your answer, in order for you at your level to be able to carry out a joint action with your counterparts from the MUP, there would have had to be some sort of coordination or planning at a higher level among representatives of the VJ and the MUP for this action to be carried out. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back to the order, I would like to look at page 5 of the English and this is page 3 in the B/C/S, it's paragraph 5.3 where the specific tasks are assigned to your unit. Do you have that before you, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In this paragraph you were tasked with settling up a blockade along the line of Crnusa, village of Prvi Tunel, and the village of Stari Trg. Are all villages located in Kosovska Mitrovica municipality, correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Correct. MS.KRAVETZ: Your Honours, in the interest of saving time I'm not going to show all these localities to the witness on the map, but they are in page-- on page 14 of P615, which is the Kosovo atlas at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And here your assignment is to support MUP forces in defeating and destroying Albanian terrorists and there are a number of different villages and localities mentioned here, Mazic, Resane, Carescani [phoen] Pasoma, these are all villages located to the south of where your units were depolyed in Vucitrn municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in your statement at paragraph 16 you referred to a -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: You asked me about the villages south of where I was, but you didn't let me respond. You see that this is copied, Bajgora, Skrovna, Samodreza, that's why we went to Pristina to clarify the part that does not relate to the 58th Brigade, but rather has to do with item 5.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the interpretation was correct, you said this was copied, Bajgora and Bare. You mean that these localities were outside of your specific area of deployment, is that -- if I'm understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're understanding me correctly but you misinterpreted what I said, Bajgora, Skrovna, Samodreza, that's not in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Bajgora was not in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. That axis, Madam, Bajgora-Skrovna-Samodreza is outside. Bajgora as a village, yes, but this axis diverges from the axis mentioned here Stari Trg, Bare, Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My question, my initial question which is very simple, I just wanted to know, for you to confirm if all these villages were to the south of where you were deployed and you said that that was correct. Now, in paragraph --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. In paragraph 16 you referred to an operative report that you sent on 23rd April, this is 5D1129, where you report on preparation for coordination with the MUP to implement the tasks that are indicated here in this order. And I would like to know, Colonel, how was this coordination between you and MUP forces carried out in order to fulfil the tasks that were assigned to you in this order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I'll point out right away that throughout the war I had excellent cooperation with this detachment. The commander of the detachment would come to my command post or I would go to his command post --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: May I interrupt you just to ask for a clarification. Which detachment specifically are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: The 35th Detachment of the PJP's. It was Branko Prljevic, Colonel Branko Prljevic, who was their commander. Regardless of the place, we met on a daily basis, studied this task that we had been issued with in the order. We would go to carry out reconnaissance of that axis, and then based on the reconnaissance we would issue our own decision. He for his units and I for my units, and we would go to Pristina. He would report to General Obradovic -- rather, Obrad Stevanovic, and I would report I think it was Colonel Stefanovic who was in the command, and we would receive approval for our idea as to how this order should be implemented. So we would go together. While carrying out the task, on one occasion on the 30th of April we were visited by Colonel Stefanovic from the army, and on the 1st of May I think my colleague in the 35th Detachment received a visit from General Obrad Stevanovic. And they were satisfied with our engagement, our mutual coordination, and cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in this specific instance with regard to the order that we're looking at now, you went to Pristina to consult with Colonel Stefanovic and your counterpart, the commander of the 35th PJP Detachment spoke to Obrad Stevanovic in order to be able to implement this task? Am I understanding your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, we do not consult our superior. We go to present our decision and seek approval for its implementation. We report on the coordination we have achieved, and his superior for the PJP and my superior for the VJ units would approve the decision. So it was not a consultation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if this is a convenient time to interrupt for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As good as any. We have to break now, Mr. Savic, for an hour, so could you please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you again at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Judge Chowhan has been unwell and is unable to continue this afternoon, but we have decided to continue in his absence since we consider that to be in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, before the break we were discussing this order you have before you and how the implementation was carried out, and you have spoken about different units referred to in this order. Were any local civilians, armed local civilians, involved in carrying out the actions that are contemplated in this order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. As this order, there were no armed civilians. This was too serious an action and the objective was to lift the blockade of Stari Trg, which was an important feature of state interest. This was a mine that cannot operate properly because there were permanent attacks from Bajgora, Stari Trg, therefore they were none. No other forces apart from this detachment and units from my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you is that because in the order there you have before you if you look at number 2 of the order, I believe this is page 1 in the B/C/S version and it's page 2 on the English, if you see right under the heading Pristina Corps assignments, there's a reference to Pristina Corps together with reinforcements and the armed non-Siptar population of Kosovo and Metohija is supporting MUP forces in defeating and destroying Albanian terrorist forces. Do you see that in the order? If you look down under number 2 I believe this is the same page in the B/C/S, the almost-to-last paragraph, the last sentence says: "Armed local non-Albanians are to be assigned with guards facilities and roads and with protecting local non-Albanians." You see that, Colonel, correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is paragraph 3 of item 2, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we've had many witnesses here before you who have been asked about this expression armed non-Siptar population and who have not been able to explain what it means. When you received this order from the Pristina Corps command and I presume you read it entirely -- in its entirety, what did you understand this to mean, the armed non-Siptar population?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I was not receiving any interpretation of what you have been saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll just repeat this. What I was saying -- I'll just say very briefly. Armed non-Siptar population that is referred to in -- under number 2 in this order, what does that refer to? Who is this armed non-Siptar population that's being referred to in this order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I did not encounter these forces in my area. I saw a reference to them in the order, and I saw them marked somewhere in some sort of a unit near the village of Kosutovo or thereabouts. Other than, that military installations and facilities of vital state interest were being secured up until the 1st of May by military territorial units, that was their main objective, and they were working with MUP units on this. Therefore, I assert that in the area of responsibility of the 58th Brigade there were no non-armed Siptar persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say you saw them marked somewhere in some sort of unit near the village, which village exactly did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: This is the village of Kosutovo it straddles the Mitrovica-Zubin Potok road. There was a map that I looked at and they were marked there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: They were -- okay. So you saw this when you say you saw there was a map that was attached to the order that you received?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. We received an attachment to this order for the Bajgora-Bare action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, when you received this order and saw this reference and you saw this unit being marked on the map, did you consult or ask your commander what this meant, who this unit was that was supposed to be engaged in this village of Kosutovo I think it was that you said?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I wasn't worried and I wasn't wondering. This sector that is marked here is where my first infantry battalion from the 58th Light Infantry Brigade happened to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So the area where this persons, these non-armed Siptar -- or Albanian persons were supposed to be deployed was an area that fell within the area of responsibility of your brigade, if I'm understanding your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, I'm telling you this is what the document says, but I didn't see them on the ground. Where I saw them marked, that's true, that's where one of my battalions and the establishment happened to be on the day the document was written.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So although the map that you saw had this unit deployed in your area of responsibility, it did not occur to you ask your commander who these persons were that were supposed to carry out actions in the area of responsibility of your brigade? You had -- you did not ask any questions about who these persons that were deployed there were?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I understand your interest. Item 2 is the task of my superior command. It is logical for us to go through the entire order, but whichever commander must start this task, he will be looking at items 4 and 5 because those are the tasks for his unit. You see at 5.3 there is no reference to the armed non-Siptar component, is there?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, and is there any military facility of interest in this village of Kosutovo where this unit you're referred to was deployed, because we see in the order that they're being tasked with guarding military facilities and roads and protecting the population, the non-Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: There are no military facilities there and they're not marked there as a unit. There is actually no reference to them as a unit. There is mention there of some armed -- I'm sorry. Armed non-Siptar population, so this is not a unit. The scale for this map is 1:100 or 200.000 which I interpreted at this time was a mistake. I can't say my attention was drawn by this since, again, this was exactly in the opposite direction from the main axis of operations for my brigade Stari Trg-Bajgora. This is a peripheral area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The reason I used the word "unit" was you yourself had referred to some sort of unit near this village, that's why I was asking about this unit that you saw on the map.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I was being less than precise. This sector is marked here, this semicircle, and then this semicircle was marked in the defence area of my own battalion, which was later shifted to the Stari Trg-Bajgora axis. This is where a unit came, the name of which was the 56th Military Territorial Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So this semicircle you're referring to was also an area where the 56th Military Territorial Detachment was deployed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's move on from there. You say in your statement that the actions that are envisaged in this order were carried out during a period of approximately seven to eight days between 25th April and 1st May 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And on 1st May did your brigade or units from your brigade break through the KLA front line at Melenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Meljanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sorry for my mispronunciation.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did indeed break through their line and we joined up with units of the 354th Infantry Brigade in the Bajgora sector, Bajgora village. Meljanica village is to the left in relation to that road looking from Mitrovica in the direction of Bajgora or on the left wing of the attack front.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did your units then proceed to advance south of Meljanica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: The front line was stretching from the south-east to the north-west, and little by little, it shifted from south-west to the north-east towards Bajgora village. This is what the front line was like. If you look at the map, it went like this. And then the village of Meljanica is on the left wing of that front -- well, I'm talking in relation to my forces obviously, and there was very stubborn resistance by the enemy in that sector, the Siptar terrorist forces or whatever you want to call them. And then after the breakthrough the enemy moved north of this village and we believed that the forces moving at this point were large-scale forces, and that is why Bajgora 2 action ensued. So I'm not sure if that is sufficiently clear for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. The reason I'm asking is we've heard evidence that as a result of these operations in the Bajgora area and the ones you've shown on the map further south, the civilian population was displaced en masse to the general area of the village of Cecelija. That's correct, isn't it, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: You probably got something wrong because I don't know a single village by that name, but it was said at the time that some of the population from the Bajgora area where there were a number of villages and the main villages would be Bare Bajgora, Mazic, Vidusic, something to the effect that some of the population of Bajgora village had probably been taken to Vesekovac, Skrovna as for the rest of the population who had fled we found them later north of Mazic and those were people from Vlahinja village so that was a refugee village that I was telling you about; but I didn't tell you that at a later stage over the following ten days there were several hundreds more of those locals who were now returning to their villages. There are several daily reports talking about this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: May I stop you there. I think there's maybe an error in the transcript here. I was talking of the village of Cecelija, which is referred to in paragraph 18 of your statement I see its not been correctly transcribed in the transcript. So what I was indicating that as a result of these operations the population fled to the south of the general area of Bare and Bajgora and concentrated in the general area of the village of Cecelija. That's correct isn't it, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I was shown that portion in Cecelija, Samodreza, Skrovna, Vesekovac, for the most part it was people from Vucitrn municipality who had fled to those parts. The village you mentioned, Cecelija in relation to Mazic, well the difference between the two is 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And, Colonel, I think that you [indiscernible] something today because everyone's referring to you as General --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: General, yet again. I have my luck to thank for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, we have heard evidence in this case that on 2nd May a convoy that was travelling in Studime gorge or near the area of Gornje Sudimlje was attacked by Serb forces or that a massive attack occurred there which resulted in the death of hundreds of civilians. Did you receive any information on this event at the time when these operations were taking place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I think the interpreter is probably confusing the 2nd of May with the 2nd of June because we're talking about the 2nd of May, aren't we? I do know that it's -- it's difficult for you to pronounce all these names of these villages, Sudimlje, Sudimlje. About the refugee group I found out about these on the 2nd of May as soon as they reached the Kicic village area which is far on the right wing of this section of the front line. As soon as I had been informed by officers from that section of the front, I was off immediately to see what was going on together with the chief of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP and the commander of the 35th Detachment of the PJP. Following consultations --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... before we get sidetracked here. I was asking you specifically about this attack on a convoy that was travelling - and you've corrected my pronunciation of the location - Sudimlje gorge on 2nd of May. My question was whether you received information at the time, 2nd of May, when this occurred that there had been a massacre in which over hundred people, civilians, had been killed. That was my question. It's simply a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise for my comprehensive explanation. The answer is no I had no information indicating that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, would it be usual for you to receive no information about such an event that involved such a large-scale killing of civilians in an area where you and other units were carrying out a joint operation? Wouldn't you normally receive reports or information from the units about an event of this scale?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. This is the right-hand neighbour of the 15th Armoured Brigade, that's their area and the villages mentioned here are ahead of the front end of that brigade. And we didn't send operations reports from brigade to brigade; rather, we would send our reports to the corps command. One thing that was of relevance to all the units, the corps command would then report back to them including my brigade and this was the case with Vlahinja where all of the corps's units were informed on what to do with the refugee group found there. So this is something that happens to be in territory that was not under our control, not under the control of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you didn't see any mention of this massacre in any of the reports that you received from the corps command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I first found out about this in 2000 when investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor came to Serbia while it was still Serbia and Montenegro at the time and they asked me certain questions about that massacre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So prior to that date you had received no information about this event?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in your statement at paragraph 33 you refer to a group of civilians that you encountered in the general region of Kicici village and you said you went to that location, you contacted the SUP chief and commander of the PJP Detachment. This was a group predominantly of women, children, elderly, that's correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you get any information from this large group, you're talking about a group of 2.000 or 3.000 people that you and your units encountered there, any information from where they were coming from? I mean, how did they end up in that region of Kicici village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I received no information at the time. They were exhausted. They had obviously been on the road for quite some time, and we proposed that they put themselves up in Kicic village which they accepted. According to an order by the corps commander, we were supposed to forestall any movements by civilians in areas of combat activity and we were supposed to help them go back to where they come from. You see, Kicic village happened to be my area, and several days later because it was quite obvious to us at the time that the area was overcrowded some of those people were transferred to other neighbouring villages that were vacant at the time and had been abandoned, Dobra Luka, for example, another village that was outside of my area of responsibility. Area of responsibility, there you have a military term, right, but what I'm trying to say is they left the area which I controlled at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, and you say these were mostly women, children, and elderly. Where were the men?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: And the elderly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What had happened to the men?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I spent about an hour there. The fighting was still going on. It's the 2nd of May, you see, there was still operations that were afoot and there were clashes going on with the Siptar terrorist forces. One thing that mattered to me was for those people to be moved around the villages. I was a military commander. I had no special authority over those civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We have heard some evidence from a witness who was in Kicici village at this time and she recounted that she went through quite an ordeal before getting there. She was in the convoy that was attacked that we spoke about earlier, and she told the Court that she and the other survivors of this massacre were detained at an agricultural compound outside Vucitrn for some time and that later her group which was mostly women, children, the elderly were ordered to go to Kicici village. Do you know anything about this, about refugees being detained at an agricultural compound outside Vucitrn town? We're talking about the evening/early morning of 2nd or 3rd May.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. Later in 2000, as I said, I heard about these allegations. I don't know. I said it was outside my area and until my proofing for the trial started I had not been aware of those developments. But to be quite frank what I saw written there I found quite irritating.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In the evidence we've heard also from the same witness, Fedrije Xhafa, is that at this agricultural compound the men were separated from the women and children and the men were taken to a prison and you're going to excuse me for my pronunciation of the village Prekovnica prison, which is a little bit to the north of Vucitrn and that they were held there under inhumane conditions.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Prekovnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you have any information about this, about men being held separated from the rest of the refugees and taken to this detention facility in early May?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. Look, Madam, I know about the detention facility in Prekovnica, that's midway between Mitrovica and Vucitrn, but the prisons are not under the authority of the MUP. I think it's the Ministry of Justice actually that's in charge of prisons. Therefore, I have no information indicating what exactly went on there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, Colonel. We'll move on to a different topic. In your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was all of that about the same event? There weren't two separate massacres on the 2nd of May --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: No, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's the one event.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same event at paragraphs 72(m) and (i) of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Colonel, moving on to a completely different topic. You told us earlier that in 1998 you were head of Combat Group 3 of the 15th Brigade, 15th Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said your commander was Colonel Cirkovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was then and still is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in August of 1998 you carried out a series of joint actions with the MUP; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The area of responsibility of the 15th Armoured Brigade was in the Vucitrn area, as we saw earlier. Was that also the case in 1998, Vucitrn municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. Vucitrn municipality was in the zone of responsibility of the 125th Motorised Brigade. We were in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So at the time you were in the municipality of Pristina, that's correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In 1998, in August 1998, were you -- were carrying out these joint operations with the MUP. Did you hear or see any reference to orders of the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I may have told the Defence I received orders from the brigade commander directly. We had round-the-clock contact. He brought me written orders and issued me with oral orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But isn't it correct, Colonel, that the joint actions that were carried out by your brigade with the MUP were coordinated and planned and ordered by the Joint Command in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: It's possible, but I received orders exclusively from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to show you a document this is P1423 and it's a report on combat tasks carried out by the 15th Brigade. It's signed by your commander at the time, Colonel Cirkovic. If we could have that up in e-court. P1423, yes. So I would like to draw your attention to number 1 in the B/C/S version, the first sentence where it says: "Between 25th July and 6th August, 1998, MUP units were engaged by decision of the joint command for Kosovo and Metohija," do you see that and it indicates the locations or areas of deployment where this engagement took place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the last sentence of paragraph 1 says: "Previous operations by MUP and VJ units were carried out with the knowledge and approval of the joint command for Kosovo and Metohija and there was no deviation from orders."

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, this document was shown to me during my proofing. I was the commander of Combat Group 3, which is equivalent to a battalion. What the brigade commander reports to the corps commander is something that is far from the eyes and knowledge of a battalion commander. So it's not for me to comment on and interpret a document issued by my superior, what he meant to say by it concerning reporting up the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well. So I take it from your evidence that at the time you had no information that the actions that you were engaging together with the MUP had been ordered by the Joint Command, despite what your commander here is reporting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well. I want to move on to a different topic. During your testimony today you were asked whether you took any measures with regard to ordinary soldiers, disciplinary measures, and you referred to -- your answer was yes and you said that sometimes 15, as many as 30 soldiers, were in detention due to different disciplinary infractions that they had committed. Now, these infractions that you're referring to that resulted in the arrest of -- or detention of these persons, soldiers, were minor infractions; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you're basically talking about infractions such as abandonment of post -- you have no -- are you getting interpretation now, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: But with interruptions. Sometimes I hear it but sometimes there are interruptions in it. We've come to the minor infractions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. I'll repeat my question, and please let me know if you don't get interpretation in your headphones. So what I was asking was, so the detention that you ordered with respect to these soldiers that you referred to earlier was for infractions such as abandonment of post, failure to comply with an order, there were things like that, minor infractions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 36 of your statement you refer to a report, unfortunately we don't have the translation although I think part of it was used today. And you say: "In the period from 15th May, 1999, 18 persons were arrested for the commission of crimes." Were these also similar types of crimes, minor infractions, committed by soldiers in your unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Concerning these 18 persons, I saw that in the operative reports and criminal reports were filed against them. These were thefts or looting. Thefts are the milder form and looting is the more serious form. We sent criminal reports to the military court in Pristina, and then to ease the workload, part of these infractions were processed in the district court in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And theft and looting was a widespread problem in your brigade, was it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: In view of the number of instances we see here, one might say that there was a lot of that, but in view of the overall situation as regards breaches of discipline or the law, it was not drastic. When we talk about the most serious crimes, such as murder or rape, such things did not happen in the brigade. This refers mainly to the taking of property from abandoned houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand your evidence correctly, none of these 18 persons were investigated or prosecuted for any serious crimes such as murder or rape?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question properly. As regards these 18, misdemeanour and criminal measures were taken against them. I said there had been no murders or rapes in the brigade and the units that were later subordinated to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Colonel, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour, and I think I ran out of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of your statement you refer to supporting the MUP forces in the action Slup i Voksa. Now, is that in Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In that area and the surrounding parts, were you aware of a particular problem of looting in August 1998?
